image_description: A close-up shot of a white Apple iPod Classic held in a person's hand. The device features the characteristic rectangular shape with rounded corners, a color LCD screen on the upper half displaying a music library interface with text and album art, and the iconic circular click wheel with a central button on the lower half. White earphone cables are plugged into the top of the device. The background is blurred, showing indistinct shapes.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The text displayed on the iPod screen is illegible gibberish/simulated characters rather than clear, readable font. While common in AI generations, it fails to accurately render a realistic UI.
The central button lacks the distinct physical separation or shadow depth usually present, appearing slightly fused or flat against the surrounding ring.
The connection point of the white headphone cables to the top of the iPod is vague and structurally unclear; the plugs seem to merge into the casing without a defined port.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific model generation (Classic vs Nano vs Touch) and verify class alignment.
To analyze the severity of the text gibberish and determine if it constitutes a critical failure in UI rendering.
To check for boundary bleeding between the click wheel components and the main body, and verify the integrity of the casing edges.
To assess the physical plausibility of the cable connections and the depth relationship between the hand and the device.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of on-screen text/UI elements
Physical definition of the click wheel buttons (center vs ring)
Connection geometry of the headphone jacks at the top edge
Edge sharpness of the device against the hand background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact. In product photography, UI legibility is key. Does the gibberish significantly detract from the 'realism' of the object? Also, verify if the click wheel looks like a single molded piece or distinct mechanical parts, as AI often blends these.
